Title: 3 Habits to Beat Rainy Day Fatigue (It's Not Laziness)

Description:
Feel drained and foggy on cloudy, rainy days? It's not laziness - your hormones and blood vessels are reacting to the weather. Less sunlight means less serotonin, the hormone that keeps you feeling alert. Falling barometric pressure dilates blood vessels in your brain and triggers a burst of serotonin - nearly 3 in 4 migraine sufferers name falling pressure as their top weather trigger. And low pressure nudges your body toward rest mode, dropping your blood pressure and leaving you sluggish even after a full night's sleep.

Get bright light first thing in the morning, even under clouds, keep a consistent sleep and wake time, and stay ahead with light exercise on gloomy days.
